body: A CoAP client on a real socket, so that something other than our own loopback can be the thing that answers it.

author: blu
body: Milliseconds per PIT tick, and the poll budget between clock reads. The budget is what makes a retransmission possible at all: the endpoint only retransmits when it is ticked past its deadline, so the receive poll has to give up periodically rather than block for the whole interaction.

author: blu
body: Put every datagram the endpoint asked for on the wire. A step can emit more than one -- a separate response is acknowledged while the answer is being delivered -- so this is a loop and not a send.

author: blu
body: One round: wait for a datagram, and if none comes before the poll budget is spent, advance the endpoint's clock instead. Those are the only two things that can move a CoAP interaction forward, and both are here so that a lost request is retransmitted by the same loop that would have delivered the answer.
